title: STRANGE MINUTE · WHAT IF #12
endSub: Would you trust it with Earth?

lines.text: What if we punched an asteroid off course?

lines.say: NASA actually did it. In twenty twenty-two.

lines.text: The target was Dimorphos. About 530 feet wide.
lines.say: The target was Dimorphos. About five hundred thirty feet wide.

lines.text: It circles a bigger asteroid called Didymos.
The probe, DART, was about the size of a vending machine.
It slammed in at about 14,000 miles per hour.
lines.say: It slammed in at about fourteen thousand miles per hour.
Almost seven million miles from Earth.

lines.text: NASA hoped to change its orbit by 73 seconds.
lines.say: NASA hoped to change its orbit by seventy-three seconds.
It changed it by thirty-two minutes.

lines.text: The hit blasted out a rock tail thousands of miles long.
Now Europe's Hera probe went to see the crater.
So if a big one ever heads our way...
We might just knock it aside. Would you trust it with Earth?

NASA really did it — and it worked better than planned. ☄️ Would you trust it with Earth? 👇

youtube.first_comment: If a giant asteroid headed for Earth — would you trust a punch like this? ☄️👇

sources: NASA DART: impact Sept 26, 2022 on Dimorphos (~160 m / ~530 ft), moonlet of Didymos; ~6.1 km/s (~14,000 mph); ~11 million km (~7 million mi) from Earth
NASA: orbit period cut by ~32 min (11 h 55 min → 11 h 23 min); minimum success threshold 73 s; ejecta tail >10,000 km
ESA Hera (launched Oct 2024) to inspect the impact site at Didymos in late 2026 (news Nov 2026: arrival)
